conversationalSummary.text: For TODAY, it’s probably not worth chasing—there’s no really reliable window and the wind setup looks poor for Rey Cortiço, so it could get messy fast. I’d check Surfline and MEO Beachcam before leaving, and only bother heading out if they look noticeably better than what this is hinting. With low rising tide you might catch something on the sandbanks, but overall confidence is low, so I’d save the drive.

best.explanation: Rey Cortiço looks like a small north coast window for Rare window, Low confidence: 0.3-0.6 m, 51 kJ, 8 s period, lully 28/100, and wind is the main risk.  An open beach break where the sandbanks decide everything; this is best for quiet, punchy peaks when Lagide is too small; 6-9s at low tide can still work on Belgas if the sandbars are lined up, so checking exposed beaches makes sense.  Watch: Surfline consistency is lully; wind angle is poor for this spot.
best.shortExplanation: Rey Cortiço is worth a quick check for after work (16:30 start), but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide should let the sandbars work without overdoing it.
warnings: wind angle is poor for this spot
